capitals.name: Tara
capitals.note: Infobox capital; the page says Mide 'originally referred to the area around the Hill of Uisneach'. No years are given for any seat.

correction.text: 'At its greatest extent, it included all of County Meath and County Westmeath' and parts of Offaly, Longford, Cavan, Dublin, Kildare and Louth

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Meath. The page says the kingdom existed 'from the 1st to the 12th century AD' and that the Ui Neill took the area in 'the fourth and fifth centuries'; it gives no area. The partial counties are left out, so the shape is the core only. In the 11th and 12th centuries Mide was 'frequently overrun and partitioned'.

region.text: Mide, taken by the Ui Neill from the Laigin

ledger.note: The Ui Neill take Mide. The Ui Neill 'came from Connacht and pushed out the Laigin' in 'the fourth and fifth centuries' and the Kings of Mide came to dominate the Southern Ui Neill kindreds; 400 is a rounding (confidence 1). The Leinster page says the Southern Ui Neill took the Kingdom of Meath from the Laigin.

region.text: Meath, awarded to Hugh de Lacy as the Lordship of Meath

ledger.note: 1172: Henry II awards Meath to Hugh de Lacy. 'In 1172, the kingdom was awarded to Hugh de Lacy as the Lordship of Meath' by Henry II as Lord of Ireland; the Ua Mael Sechlainn (O'Melaghlin) dynasty was 'forced west and settled on the east bank of the River Shannon'.
1172: the kingdom of Meath ends. The page's infobox gives the Norman grant of 1172 as its end; the Norman invasion article has Henry allow de Lacy 'to take royal troops into Meath' in early 1172.

wars.name: Norman invasion of Meath
wars.outcome: Meath granted to Hugh de Lacy by Henry II in 1172.
wars.note: Ruaidri Ua Conchobair later 'drove the Normans out of Meath' and burned Trim and Kells (Ruaidri's page, undated).

certainty.note: The page gives only the counties; the kingdom was 'frequently overrun and partitioned' in its last two centuries.

sources.title: Kingdom of Meath
sources.note: Identity, Ui Neill origin, extent, 1172 grant.

sources.title: Lordship of Ireland
sources.note: The unconquered kingdom of Meath granted to Hugh de Lacy.

notes: Start 400 is a rounding of 'the fourth and fifth centuries'; the Mide province 'is traditionally said to have been created by Tuathal Techtmar' in the first century. Brega (the Ui Enechglaiss were expelled across the Wicklow Mountains in the early 6th century), the Kings of Tara and the High Kingship alternation with the Northern Ui Neill are not territorial events on the page and are not in the ledger. The Lordship of Meath (de Lacy) is inside the Lordship of Ireland dossier.
